code.why: The RTMP ingest's dialect: the kernel's live media calls it for a publisher on the ingest's side port, which the pack's server serves beside its HTTP host (server.ts, serveStream over fetch.ingest). A walk speaks HTTP, sockets and line protocols to the pack's fetch; no journey step speaks RTMP yet (the walk has no RTMP client over a recorded clip), so no walk publishes, and the story's broadcast (OBS going live, a bandwidth test, the stream's end) is the encoder's act outside the walk. Walked by hand with ffmpeg's RTMP publisher in the kernel's own evidence (architecture, Other wires: live media).

A live stream as Get Streams answers it: a stream exists only from an encoder's RTMP publish (semantics/live.ts started), which no walk can make (the walk has no RTMP client); every Get Streams a walk asks answers the empty list.
A title or category changed while the channel is live, shown on its stream: the stream exists only from an encoder's RTMP publish, which no walk can make (the walk has no RTMP client).
How long a live stream has been on, drawn only while the channel is live: a stream exists only from an encoder's RTMP publish, which no walk can make (the walk has no RTMP client).

The World's audience door sets how many people watch a live stream: a stream exists only from an encoder's RTMP publish, which no walk can make, so the door has nothing to set in a walk (the life's audience arrives with the broadcast, outside the walk).

The account a sign-up door names again: the World's credential door (POST /_twin/console) is called at every boot and answers the same account and app when the password is its own, else refuses the taken login; a walk calls it once.
The serve seam the World's host runs: the HTTP listener and the RTMP ingest on its side port around the pack's fetch; a walk calls the fetch directly.
